model_conventions.source_locator: NBER PDF pages 6-8; extraction lines 351-354 and 397-438
model_conventions.formal_meaning: Task productivity gamma(i) and the equilibrium rental rate are positive when converting gamma(i) comparisons with W/R into direct unit-cost comparisons between R and W/gamma(i).
model_conventions.why_needed: The paper calls gamma(i) productivity, divides by it in the unit-cost formula, and uses W/R in equation (6), but the displayed Assumption 1 states monotonicity without a separate positivity clause.
model_conventions.unresolved_relation_to_literal_source: This is an explicit economic-domain reading of the model primitives, not an additional claimed theorem of Assumption 1.

checked_proof_steps.source_step: Strictly increasing gamma and gamma(I-tilde)=W/R divide tasks at I-tilde; technological feasibility truncates the division at I, yielding I*=min{I,I-tilde}.
checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: Below min{I,I-tilde}, automation is available and R<W/gamma(i); above it, either i>I or W/gamma(i)<R.

checked_proof_steps.source_step: Solve B9, s_L dlnW +(1-s_L)dlnR=dlnY|K,L, together with B10, dlnW-dlnR=q.
checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: dlnW=dlnY|K,L +(1-s_L)q and dlnR=dlnY|K,L-s_L q; for automation q=-d this yields the productivity-minus-displacement wage formula and a positive rental change when both components and the labor share are nonnegative.

defects.source_locator: NBER PDF page 13 (PDF page 15); extraction lines 736-739 loses the bars
defects.source_claim: The NBER PDF states that there exists K-bar > K-underbar such that automation raises the wage for K<K-bar and lowers it for K>K-bar.
affected_source_locators: Assumption 3, NBER PDF page 8 / extraction line 445
Proposition 3, NBER PDF page 13 / extraction lines 736-739
defects.repair_obligation: Either prove the literal NBER ordering and both wage-sign regions under Assumptions 1-3, or obtain an explicit maintainer-approved corrected target. The later AER inequality is not source authority for this formalization.
defects.acceptance_condition: A Lean proof of the literal NBER clause, or a pinned and explicitly approved corrected statement that records archival_equivalence_claimed=false.
defects.resolution_evidence: Visual inspection of the pinned NBER PDF confirms K-bar > K-underbar. Assumption 3 imposes K<K-underbar, so its conjunction with the stated negative-wage region K>K-bar is unavailable inside the proposition's advertised assumption set.
defects.status_impact_rationale: This is a material unproved clause of Proposition 3, and no corrected target has been approved.

policy: Review source proof text by exact source locator and mathematical claim; Lean declaration names are navigation only and are not evidence.
Give every defect a stable unique id using letters, digits, dot, underscore, or hyphen so source-map contracts can route its repair without depending on Lean names.
A source proof defect is not a paper/model assumption. Do not classify its repaired conclusion as validated_source_assumption.

Record every explicit formalization convention that resolves a source-model ambiguity in model_conventions, with the literal source relation and checked scope. A convention is not a literal source theorem without a source-side semantic bridge.

Record every source proof step independently checked by Lean in checked_proof_steps, including its exact source step, checked conclusion, and scope. A finite/event-level step does not silently establish an arbitrary-space, pointwise-conditioning, or arbitrary-partition claim.

For every defect, record the mathematical repair obligation and acceptance condition. Resolve it by a Lean derivation, leave it as an explicit open proof obligation, or record an explicit corrected source statement.

For every defect, separately record status_impact and status_impact_rationale. statement_impact says which source text changed; status_impact says whether the issue is a formalized note, a substantial source-paper caveat with a fully proved correction, or a partial-formalization boundary.

A proof-only defect may coexist with a source-faithful final theorem only after the replacement derivation is proved. A minor source-statement repair may also be formalized_note when the substantive advertised endpoint is unchanged. Only a substantial central source-paper error with a fully proved corrected endpoint justifies formalized_with_caveat.
